title: Approve terminology + positioning for streaming, tool calling, and structured output in Hosted API docs
creator: Nikhil Sharma
description:
Context
We are refreshing developer-facing examples and docs across SDKs and redwood-docs. Prior feedback from Solutions Eng + Support shows confusion caused by inconsistent naming ("function calling" vs "tools"), unclear guarantees around JSON outputs, and ambiguous streaming event semantics.

This ticket locks the public terminology + positioning to use across:
- Streaming guide + API reference callouts
- Tool calling docs (definitions, parallel tools, tool result messages)
- Structured output guide (JSON schema constraints + validation)
- Changelog/migration notes + compatibility notes (OpenAI-compat)

Goals
- One consistent mental model + vocabulary across docs and SDK examples.
- Reduce support load from customers expecting stronger guarantees than we provide.
- Align messaging with Hosted API roadmap: clear about what’s supported today, what’s “model-dependent”, and what’s “Redwood-verified”.

Non-goals
- Changing protocol semantics or the API surface.
- Rewriting the entire docs IA (handled in docs PRs + migration notes).

Proposed terminology (decision required)
1) Streaming
- Primary term: “Streaming responses”
- Avoid: “token streaming” as a guarantee. (We stream incremental deltas; unit may be tokens or token-like segments depending on model/runtime.)
- Phrase to use: “incremental output deltas over a streaming connection”
- What we will promise in docs: stable event types and a deterministic way to assemble a final message from deltas.

2) Tool calling
- Primary term: “Tool calling”
- Secondary/alias: “Function calling” (only as an interoperability alias; note we implement OpenAI-style tool calling semantics.)
- Avoid: “plugins” in API docs (too overloaded).
- Key wording: “The model can request one or more tool calls; your app executes tools and sends tool results back as messages.”

3) Structured output
- Primary term: “Structured output (JSON schema)”
- Alternate term allowed once per page: “schema-constrained JSON output”
- Avoid: “JSON mode” (implies always-valid JSON without validation/retry; historically a source of confusion).
- Guarantee language:
  - “Best effort unless explicitly stated otherwise for a given model family.”
  - “Always validate and implement retry/fallback.”

Positioning guidance (copy blocks to standardize)
A) Streaming positioning (short)
“Use streaming responses when you want lower perceived latency and real-time UI updates. Streaming delivers partial deltas as they’re generated, plus a final completion event. Your app should assemble a final message from deltas and handle disconnects/retries.”

B) Tool calling positioning (short)
“Tool calling lets the model ask your application to run tools (APIs, DB queries, workflows). The model returns a tool call request with a tool name + JSON arguments. Your app executes tools and sends tool results back, then the model continues.”

C) Structured output positioning (short)
“Structured output lets you request JSON that matches a provided schema. Because models can still produce invalid JSON in edge cases (especially during streaming), validate outputs and retry or fall back when validation fails.”

What to be explicit about (to reduce surprises)
- Model variability: Tool calling + schema adherence is model-dependent; docs must not imply uniform guarantees across the entire catalog.
- Streaming edge cases: Tool call arguments can arrive incrementally; customers must buffer and only parse arguments when complete.
- Parallel tool calls: The model may request multiple tool calls in a single assistant turn; examples should show executing in parallel where safe.
- Compatibility: Our OpenAI-compat layer is close but not identical; docs should link to compatibility notes instead of burying differences.

Required output of this ticket
1) Final decision on preferred public terms + aliases.
2) “Do / Don’t” language for each feature (streaming/tools/structured output) that docs + SDK READMEs can copy.
3) A short deprecation/migration note for older docs/snippets that say “function calling” or “JSON mode”.

Acceptance criteria
- Elliot/Wei confirm docs pages adopt the agreed terms.
- Monica/Ibrahim confirm SDK examples match the same terms in comments/logging.
- Support/SE confirm the guarantee language matches what they tell customers (no overpromising).

Stakeholders
- PM: Henry Cho (owner), Nikhil Sharma
- Docs: Elliot Price, Wei Chen
- SDK parity: Ibrahim Khan
- Semantics review: Brian Murphy
- Support input: Dev Patel, Markus Klein

References
- PM-413: structured output support matrix by model
- ENG-4826: redwood-docs updates for streaming/tool calling
- Support synthesis: top issues around partial args and JSON parse failures
decision_summary:
Approved.
- Public terms: “Streaming responses”, “Tool calling”, “Structured output (JSON schema)”.
- Allowed aliases: “function calling” only as an interoperability note; “schema-constrained JSON” allowed once per page.
- Prohibited/avoid: “JSON mode” as the primary term; “token streaming” as a guarantee; “plugins” in API docs.
- Guarantee language: model-dependent; always validate; document fallbacks; no implication of strict JSON validity without validation/retry.
migration_note_copy:
Migration note for docs/snippets:
- We previously used “function calling” in some docs and SDK examples. We now use “tool calling” everywhere for consistency. “Function calling” may still appear as an alias in compatibility sections.
- We previously used “JSON mode” informally. We now use “structured output (JSON schema)” and explicitly recommend validation + retry/fallback because schema adherence is model-dependent.
notes_for_docs_team:
Implementation notes for docs pages:
- First mention on a page: use the primary term. If introducing the alias, do it immediately after first mention (e.g., “tool calling (sometimes called function calling)”).
- Add a short “Guarantees + model variability” callout box to tool calling + structured output pages.
- Streaming page: include a callout that deltas may split JSON and tool args; parse only after completion.
- Link out to OpenAI-compat differences instead of duplicating per-page.
comments: 2025-02-06 (Henry Cho): Drafted terminology proposal based on Support/SE notes and recent prospect questions. Requesting Docs + SDK parity review before we ship updated examples.
2025-02-07 (Elliot Price): Docs team aligned on “tool calling” as primary. Request: provide exact guarantee language we can put into callout boxes; avoid “token streaming” phrasing.
2025-02-10 (Dev Patel): +1 to removing “JSON mode”. Many SUP tickets are customers assuming JSON validity without validation. Strongly recommend docs show validation + retry patterns.
2025-02-11 (Ibrahim Khan): SDK examples will use the same terms in logs/README comments. We’ll also standardize on “deltas” + “final message assembly” language across Python/TS/Go.
2025-02-13 (Wei Chen): Proposed adding a “Model-dependent behavior” section to structured output page with a link to the support matrix (PM-413).
2025-02-18 (Nikhil Sharma): Approved the final terminology + positioning. Please ensure public docs do not imply strict guarantees beyond the model support matrix. Marking Done.
